title: Microsoft Teams: Workflows template adds tag members to channels automatically
summary: Hold because the data-policy path stops before connector configuration and tag permissions omit documented exceptions. The page also incorrectly treats general workflow ownership and governance rules as undocumented. The rollout dates and optional default agree with Microsoft's notice.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app.
claims.quote: We are introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Once configured, the workflow automatically adds users to selected channels whenever they are added to the associated team tag.
claims.quote: Once configured, the workflow runs whenever a user is added to the tag, eliminating the need to add members to each channel manually.

claims.claim: Team owners can choose to configure the workflow.
claims.quote: Team owners can configure the workflow at any time if desired.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: nothing changes by default and the optional template does not run until someone configures it.
claims.quote: Nothing changes by default. The template is optional and does not run until someone in a team configures it.

claims.claim: Microsoft requires no administrative action for this change.
claims.quote: No action is required.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes location-based and project-based groups with tags corresponding to sites, regions or projects as use cases.
claims.quote: This is especially useful for location-based or project-based groups where tags correspond to specific sites, regions, or projects

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice specifies standard channels and shared channels shared with everyone on the team as the applicable channel types.
claims.quote: This applies to channels that all team members can access by default: standard channels and shared channels that are shared with everyone on the team.

claims.claim: The affected users are team owners who configure the workflow and Teams users added to tags associated with configured workflows.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams users who are added to team tags associated with configured workflows.- Team owners who choose to configure the workflow.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Teams admin center path Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block reaches the app availability control.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps.
2. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the Workflows app's tenant-wide Allow or Block control.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams app allow block tenant API PowerShell Workflows app availability publishingState; Teams app block Set-CsTeamsApp. Opened Manage apps, teamsAppDefinition and beta teamsAppSettings. No supported operation for this control was found.

claims.claim: The Workflows app must be enabled in the Teams admin center for flows created through its functionality to work.
claims.quote: The Workflows app must be enabled in the Microsoft Teams admin center in order for this functionality to work.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Blocking access to the Workflows app is an app-wide control rather than a control for this single template.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control access to all types of agents and apps that are used across your organization.

claims.claim: Teams Administrator is the documented role for using the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: Security > Data and privacy > Data policy is the path to the control that configures which connectors flows may use.
claims.quote:
From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
Proceed through the steps described in Walkthrough: Create a data policy
claims.fix: Replace the UI path with 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business'. State in the note that this route classifies a selected connector as Business, matching the PowerShell example. The current path ends at the policy list, before the editing and connector-classification choices documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorToBusinessDataGroup -PolicyName <policy name> -ConnectorName <connector name> classifies the connector as Business in a data policy.
claims.quote:
Sets a connector to the business data group of a data loss policy.
Add-ConnectorToBusinessDataGroup -PolicyName e25a94b2-3111-468e-9125-3d3db3938f13 -ConnectorName shared_office365users

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell operation for the tenant Who can manage tags setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Who can manage tags" Graph API PowerShell tenant setting; Teams tenant tagging settings Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration AllowTagging WhoCanManageTags. Opened Manage tags and beta teamwork; no operation for this tenant setting was found.

claims.claim: The cited Manage tags page says PowerShell cannot manage tags.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control how tags are used across your organization in the Microsoft Teams admin center. You can’t use PowerShell to manage tags.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The execution account used by this specific template has not been stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Join member to channel" account; Workflows owner connections Teams. Opened Create flows in Microsoft Teams, Share a cloud flow and Manage flows in Microsoft Teams; read MC1540351. No template-specific execution account was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said who owns the flow created through the Workflows app.
claims.quote: Add or remove other owners (but not the flow's creator), including guest users.
claims.fix: Narrow 'Microsoft has not said which account the workflow runs as or who owns the flow' to 'Microsoft has not documented which account this template uses for its connections.' General cloud-flow ownership is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/create-team-flows, and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/teams/teams-app-home documents the Owners column for identifying the users who own a Workflows flow.

claims.claim: Flow ownership affects who can edit or stop the automation and its continuity when an owner leaves.
claims.quote:
Any owner of a cloud flow can perform these actions:
- Manage the properties of the flow (for example, start or stop the flow, add owners, or update credentials for a connection).
- Edit the definition of the flow
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/create-team-flows for ownership, edit and stop permissions, and the documented consequences of an owner leaving.

claims.claim: After configuration, membership additions are automatic rather than separately approved by a person each time.
claims.quote: When configured, the workflow will automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag.

claims.claim: An accidental tag addition changes channel membership straight away.
claims.quote: Searched: "Join member to channel" immediately; "Join member to channel" approval. Read MC1540351 and Create flows in Microsoft Teams. The notice says automatically and promptly, but specifies no immediate processing guarantee or latency.
claims.fix: Replace 'A tag added by mistake changes channel membership straight away' with 'Adding someone to the tag by mistake can trigger an unintended channel addition.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice does not specify what happens to channel membership when a user is removed from the tag.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tag workflow removed channel. Read the full MC1540351 notice and opened Manage tags and Create flows in Microsoft Teams. The notice describes additions only; no removal behaviour for this template was found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Support for targeting channel types beyond the types specified in MC1540351 is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Join member to channel when user is added to tag"; Teams tag workflow connector when. Read MC1540351 and opened Create flows in Microsoft Teams and Shared channels. No additional supported channel types were found for this template.

claims.claim: Channel membership is currently something owners keep in step by hand as groups change.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams channel membership manual owners tags. Read MC1540351, Manage tags and Teams and channels overview excerpts. The notice says this template eliminates manual additions, not that channel membership generally requires manual maintenance.
claims.fix: Remove 'Channel membership is currently something owners keep in step by hand as groups change.' The following sentence already explains the planned change without making an unsupported general claim about existing behaviour.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described the app, data-policy or tag-management controls as governing this template.
claims.quote: Facebook and Twitter connectors are altogether blocked from being used in any app or flow in non-test environments such as production or default environments.
claims.fix: Remove 'None is described by Microsoft as governing this template, so confirm each against the template once it is documented.' The documented data-policy scope includes flows in the default environment, where Learn says Workflows-created flows reside; a separate template-specific confirmation is not needed for that general scope.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm the template is permitted if the organisation plans to use it.
claims.quote: If your organization plans to use this template, we recommend reviewing your Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that it is permitted.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Setting the tenant Who can manage tags value controls who can manage the triggering tags without a team-level override qualification.
claims.quote: When you turn on this setting, team owners can set whether team members can create and manage tags within a team and the value of the Who can manage tags setting is the default value for each team.
claims.fix: Add to the existing tag-control note and the Before rollout tag-setting bullet: 'If Team owners can change who can manage tags is enabled, Who can manage tags is the default for each team and team owners can change it; when that setting is off, it cannot be changed per team.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-tags.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether Who can manage tags also controls who can configure this workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: "Who can manage tags" "workflow" configure. Read Manage tags, Create flows in Microsoft Teams and MC1540351. No statement linking this tenant tag setting to permission to configure this template was found.
